items.q: Autism diagnosis requires which two domains?
o: Social communication deficits plus restricted repetitive patterns including sensory features
items.exp: Both DSM domains must be present early (sensory reactivity sits inside restricted repetitive domain); intellectual and language abilities are specifiers, not requirements, since autism spans all IQ.
r: Incorrect. Language and IQ vary independently.
Correct. Social communication plus restricted patterns.
Incorrect. That mixes Tourette and OCD.
Incorrect. Those define ADHD.
items.kp: Social difference plus repetition equals autism core.

items.q: ADHD symptom onset and setting requirements are what?
o: Before 12, in two or more settings with impairment
items.exp: DSM requires several symptoms before twelve, cross situational pervasiveness (parent and teacher evidence) and functional impairment, excluding better explanations like sleep apnoea or trauma hypervigilance.
r: Incorrect. Adult diagnosis still traces childhood onset.
Correct. Before twelve, two settings.
Incorrect. Single setting suggests situational causes.
Incorrect. Exam only is anxiety pattern.
items.kp: Two settings, before twelve: ADHD rule.

items.q: First line medication class for moderate severe ADHD in children over 5 (local guidance) is what, with which monitoring?
o: Stimulants (methylphenidate class); pulse, BP, weight, height, cardiac history
items.exp: Stimulants give largest effect sizes; monitoring covers appetite and growth, cardiovascular parameters, tics, sleep and misuse or diversion in adolescents. Atomoxetine suits tics, anxiety or stimulant intolerance alternatives.
r: Incorrect. Atomoxetine is alternative line.
Correct. Stimulants first with cardiometabolic growth checks.
Incorrect. Antipsychotics not ADHD treatment.
Incorrect. SSRIs treat comorbidity only.
items.kp: Stimulants lead ADHD; chart pulse and growth.

o: Multiple motor plus at least one vocal tic over 1 year, onset before 18
Tics only under stress in adults
items.exp: Duration over a year with both modalities and childhood onset defines Tourette; transient tic disorder resolves within year and chronic single modality types sit between. CBIT precedes drugs for impairing tics.
r: Incorrect. Too brief and single.
Correct. Motor plus vocal, year, youth onset.
Incorrect. Vocal alone is chronic vocal tic disorder.
Incorrect. Adult stress tics need other evaluation.
items.kp: Motor and voice, a year, before eighteen.

items.q: Commonest inherited cause of intellectual disability, with large ears, long face and macro orchidism after puberty, is what?
items.exp: Fragile X (FMR1 CGG expansion) is leading inherited intellectual disability, X linked with autistic features; Down is commonest overall but chromosomal nondisjunction, not inherited pattern.
r: Correct. Fragile X inherited lead.
Incorrect. Down is commonest overall, not inherited.
Incorrect. Tuberous gives seizures and skin lesions pattern.
Incorrect. Prader Willi hyperphagia and hypotonia picture.
items.kp: Long face, big ears, fragile X.

items.q: Diagnostic overshadowing in intellectual disability means which dangerous error?
o: Attributing new psychiatric or medical symptoms to the disability itself and missing treatable illness
items.exp: Pain, depression or psychosis presenting as behaviour change gets dismissed as just their disability, delaying treatment; baseline behaviour records and physical workup counter this bias.
r: Incorrect. Autism co occurs genuinely often.
Correct. Missing illness by blaming disability.
Incorrect. Support is appropriate care.
Incorrect. Genetics not the error.
items.kp: New behaviour is illness until proven otherwise.

items.q: First line intervention for impairing Tourette tics is what?
o: Comprehensive behavioural intervention for tics (habit reversal)
items.exp: CBIT teaches awareness and competing responses with support, matching drug efficacy without metabolic harm; alpha2 agonists then antipsychotics follow severity, DBS is last resort adult refractory research care.
r: Incorrect. Drugs follow behavioural first line.
Correct. Habit reversal CBIT leads.
Incorrect. Stimulants may worsen some tics, not treat them.
Incorrect. DBS is exceptional last line.
items.kp: Train competing response before medicating tics.

items.q: Adult ADHD presentation most often emphasises what residual features?
o: Inattention, disorganisation, impulsivity and emotional dysregulation with occupational impairment
items.exp: Gross motor hyperactivity often internalises to restlessness while executive failure, missed deadlines, driving risk and substance comorbidity dominate adult morbidity; diagnosis still requires childhood onset evidence.
r: Incorrect. Hyperactivity usually attenuates outwardly.
Correct. Executive and emotional adult pattern.
Incorrect. Psychosis suggests other disorder.
Incorrect. Memory complaint is attentional, not amnesic.
items.kp: Adult ADHD forgets deadlines, not childhood.

items.q: Autism support with strongest outcome influence in childhood centres on what?
o: Early communication, educational individualisation and family support; drugs only for comorbidity
items.exp: No drug treats core autism; speech and occupational therapy, structured education, parent training and treating ADHD, anxiety, epilepsy or sleep comorbidity change trajectories. Risperidone class only targets severe irritability short term in some licences.
r: Incorrect. Core symptoms lack drug therapy.
Correct. Developmental and educational supports lead.
Incorrect. Inclusion with support is standard.
Incorrect. Restrictive diets lack cure evidence.

items.q: Stimulant treatment in ADHD with comorbid tics requires which approach?
o: Individualised trial with tic monitoring; atomoxetine or guanfacine alternatives if tics worsen
items.exp: Group data show stimulants do not worsen tics on average, so monitored trial is reasonable, switching to non stimulants if individual exacerbation occurs. Untreated ADHD often harms more.
r: Incorrect. Not absolute; monitor individually.
Correct. Trial with monitoring and alternatives ready.
Incorrect. Prophylactic antipsychotics add harm.
Incorrect. ADHD still deserves treatment.
items.kp: Tics do not automatically ban stimulants.
